identity.author: John Davenant
identity.work: Two Dissertations (De praedestinatione through Cap. X Arg. I)
identity.edition: Dissertationes duae (Cambridge: Roger Daniel, 1650). Partial through Cap. X Arg. I (Valencia/Vasquez). Further Cap. X Args remain.

scope.locus: De praedestinatione Cap. X controversy-sum + Arg. I.
scope.next_locus: Cap. X Arg. II+ (further confirmation reasons for non-election from mere will).

sections.title: Cap. X: controversy-aim — show the eternal distinction of elect and non-elect in God's mind and will had no origin or motive from antecedent foresight of good acts in Peter/Paul or opposite acts in Cain/Judas
english: So in disputing this reprobation decree we shall do one thing: show that the eternal distinction of elect and non-elect in God's mind and will had no origin, occasion, or motive of any kind from antecedent foresight of good acts in the elect — penitence, faith, and perseverance in Peter and Paul — or from antecedent foresight of the opposites in the non-elect — impenitence, unbelief, and final contumacy in Cain, Judas, and the rest. Rather, God's mere will first divided between sons infallibly ordained to share grace and glory, and those rejected or passed over as to that order.
sections.latin: De hoc igitur reprobationis decreto disputaturi, id unum agemus, ut ostendatur, Aeternam illam distinctionem electorum et non-electorum in mente et voluntate Divina non habuisse originem, occasionem, aut motivum qualecunque ex antecedanea praevisione bonorum actuum in personis electis, puta poenitentiae, fidei et perseverantiae in Petro et Paulo, et ex antecedanea praevisione oppositorum in non-electis, scilicet impoenitentiae, infidelitatis et contumaciae finalis in Caino, Juda, reliquisque; sed meram Dei voluntatem primo divisisse inter filios ad participationem gratiae et gloriae infallibiliter ordinatos, et inter rejecticios sive quoad talem ordinem praeteritos.

sections.title: Cap. X controversy-sum: if in the eternal decree some were preconceived as worthier/holier and thence predestined, Arminius wins; if considered as sinners worthy of ruin and given faith by special mercy after election, we win
english: The sum of this controversy comes to this. If in the eternal decree of election and reprobation God preconceived certain persons as worthier, better, and holier than others, and thence infallibly predestined them to life — and preconceived others as unworthier, worse, and more wicked, and thence shut them out from predestination to life — Arminius wins, we lose the cause. But if, on the contrary side, all who were predestined to life before the world's foundations were laid were considered by God as sinners worthy of everlasting ruin, to be infallibly gifted — by God's special mercy and a singular calling according to purpose — with faith, repentance, perseverance, and salvation itself, and were not foreseen before their election as determining themselves ahead of others by a right use of free choice from offered grace to conceive faith and persevere in it.
sections.latin: Huc redit summa hujus controversiae: Si in aeterno decreto electionis et reprobationis personae quaedam fuerunt a Deo praeconsideratae tanquam aliis digniores, meliores et sanctiores, atque inde ad vitam infallibiliter praedestinatae, atque e contra aliae quaedam praeconsideratae ut hisce indigniores, nequiores et improbiores, atque inde a praedestinatione ad vitam exclusae, vincit Arminius, nos causa cadimus: Si autem, ex adverso, quotquot ad vitam fuerunt ante jacta mundi fundamenta praedestinati, fuerunt a Deo considerati ut peccatores aeterno exitio digni, per specialem misericordiam Dei, et singularem quandam et secundum propositum vocationem, fide, resipiscentia, perseverantia, ipsaque salute infallibiliter donandi, non autem praevisi ante electionem suam tanquam prae aliis recto liberi arbitrii usu ex oblata gratia ad concipiendam fidem in eaque perseverandum sese determinantes.

sections.title: Cap. X controversy-sum continued: non-elect likewise considered sinners worthy of death, no worse in themselves, yet by freest will not dignified with the special mercy prepared for the elect — then Arminius falls, we obtain the cause
english: And on the other side take the non-elect — those called passed over or reprobate. They too were considered by God as sinners worthy of death. In themselves they were no worse. Yet by God's freest will they were not dignified with that same special mercy and efficacious calling which, prepared for the elect, wrought their faith, repentance, and salvation. Then Arminius sinks, and we obtain the cause.
sections.latin: Et e contra, si qui non-electi, praeteriti sive reprobati dicuntur, fuerunt etiam a Deo considerati ut peccatores morte digni, etsi in se nihilo deteriores, sed liberrima Dei voluntate minime dignati eadem speciali misericordia et efficaci vocatione quae electis praeparata fidem, resipiscentiam et salutem eorum operata est, tum succumbits Arminius, nos causam obtinemus.

sections.title: Cap. X: predestination already shown to depend on freest good pleasure, not antecedent human acts — remains to show the same of non-election/reprobation by gathering scattered reasons
english: As for predestination: many reasons have already shown that it depends on God's freest good pleasure, not on antecedent consideration of human acts. It remains to show the same of non-election or reprobation. Here we need only recall those reasons into order — as under standards — which in confirming our cause and answering the adversaries could be seen only dispersed and straggling.
sections.latin: Quod attinet ad praedestinationem, multis rationibus ostensum est, illam ex liberrimo Dei beneplacito, et non ex antecedanea consideratione humanorum actuum dependere. Restat igitur ut de non-electione sive reprobatione idem ostendatur: Nihil autem aliud hic nobis agendum erit, quam ut rationes eas quasi sub signa, et in ordinem revocemus, quae in confirmatione causae nostrae et in responsionibus ad argumenta adversariorum non nisi dispersae, et palantes conspici potuerunt.

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. I: from adversaries' own descriptions of reprobation — absolute forescience of final impenitence/unbelief presupposes the decree to reprobate, so the decree does not flow from that foresight
english: First: we can argue from the definitions or descriptions of reprobation that keep turning up among our adversaries. From those themselves it is plain: absolute forescience of final impenitence and unbelief, as to this or that singular person, presupposes the decree to reprobate — and so that decree does not flow from that foresight.
sections.latin: Primo, argumentari possumus ab illis sive definitionibus sive descriptionibus reprobationis, quae subinde occurrunt apud adversarios nostros: Nam ex hisce ipsis perspicue concludi potest, Praescientiam absolutam finalis impoenitentiae et infidelitatis, quoad hanc aut illam personam singularem, praesupponere decretum reprobandi, ac proinde hoc decretum ex illa praevisione non manare.

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. I: Gregory of Valencia — reprobation is the act whereby God firmly establishes to permit the reprobates' sins by not giving singular grace, exclude them from the kingdom, and punish eternally
english: Gregory of Valencia paints the picture this way (In Aquin. qu. 23. on reprobation, punct. 1). Reprobation, he says, is an act of the divine intellect. By it God firmly establishes that he will permit the reprobates' sins — not giving them the singular grace by which they would be freed from those sins — and for those sins will shut them out of the heavenly kingdom and punish them forever.
sections.latin: Gregorius Valentia reprobationem ita nobis depingit, In Aquin. qu. 23. de reprobatione, punct. 1. Reprobatio est actus Divini intellectus, quo firmiter statuit Deus reprobatorum peccata permittere, non dando iis singularem gratiam qua ab iis liberarentur, et propter illa eos a regno caelesti excludere, ac in aeternum punire.

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. I: will to permit unbelief and deny special grace precedes absolute forescience of lasting malice — though will to punish Judas follows foresight of sin; that order is enough for our sense of reprobate
english: But that most firm statute of divine intellect and will — to permit certain persons' sins, and not to apply the grace by which they would be freed — must be presupposed to their foreseen impenitence, unbelief, and contumacy. Those would not be foreseen as absolutely about to be if they were not permitted. So we obtain this: however the will to punish this singular person — Judas or Cain — follows foresight of sin, the will to permit his unbelief and impenitence, and the will to deny the special grace by which he would be efficaciously bent to faith and penitence, precede that absolute forescience of malice finally to endure in him. That is enough for us. We take as reprobate the one to whom God from eternity willed to deny that freeing grace, and whom he willed to permit by his own fault to harden in his sins. On the contrary we call predestined the one for whom God from eternity willed to prepare that singular freeing grace, and whom he would not permit to harden finally in his sins.
sections.latin: At firmissimum hoc Divini intellectus ac voluntatis statutum de permittendis peccatis quarundam personarum, et de non-apponenda gratia qua ab iis liberarentur, praevisae earundem impoenitentiae, infidelitati et contumaciae praesupponi debet, utpote quae non praeviderentur ut absolute futurae si non permitterentur. Hoc igitur obtinimus, Quod utcunque voluntas puniendi hanc singularem personam, puta Judam aut Cainum, subsequatur peccati praevisionem, tamen voluntas permittendi infidelitatem et impoenitentiam ejusdem, ac voluntas negandi specialem gratiam, qua ad fidem et poenitentiam efficaciter flecteretur, praecedit hanc praescientiam absolutam malitiae finaliter in eadem duraturae. At hoc nobis satis est, qui illum reprobatum intelligimus, cui Deus ab aeterno denegare voluit illam gratiam qua liberaretur, et quem permittere voluit suo vitio indurescere in peccatis suis; sicut e contra illum praedestinatum dicimus, cui Deus ab aeterno praeparare voluit illam singularem gratiam qua liberaretur, quemque permittere noluit in peccatis suis finaliter indurescere.

sections.title: Cap. X Arg. I close: Augustine — God can convert any wills; he eternally established to do so in some, not in others, by mere good pleasure; Vasquez — rejection from grace has no cause in the rejected beyond first parents' sin
english: For he who can — as Augustine says (De bono persever. cap. 8) — convert anyone's averse and adverse wills, and from eternity established to do this in some and not in others, elects and passes over, has mercy and has not mercy, not by a foreknown difference of human wills, but by the mere good pleasure of his will. Hear Vasquez: If reprobation is used for the act whereby someone is rejected by God, we speak either of rejection from God's grace, or of rejection from the kingdom of heaven. If of the former, it must be asserted that no cause is given on the rejected one's part beyond the first parent's sin (In 1. disp. 89. c. 5. p. 701). So although no one is shut out of heaven and sent to gehenna by God's judging sentence except for his own sins — yet, even this Jesuit freely confessing, all the reprobate are rejected from the predestined's grace by God's liberty, doing of his own what he wills.
sections.latin: Nam Qui potest, ut loquitur Augustinus, De bono persever. cap. 8. aversas et adversas quorumvis convertere voluntates, et hoc ab aeterno statuit in quibusdam facere, in quibusdam non facere, ille non secundum praescitam differentiam humanarum voluntatum, sed secundum merum beneplacitum suae voluntatis, eligit et praeterit, miseretur et non miseretur. Jam Vasques audiatur: Si reprobatio usurpetur pro actu quo quis rejicitur a Deo, aut loquimur de actu quo quis rejicitur a gratia Dei, aut quo rejicitur a regno caelorum. Si de priore sermo sit, asserendum est nullam causam ex parte ejus dari qui rejicitur, praeter peccatum primi parentis, In 1. disp. 89. c. 5. p. 701. Quamvis igitur nemo e caelo excludatur et in gehennam ablegetur ex sententia Dei judicantis, nisi propter peccata propria: tamen, vel hoc Jesuita ultro confitente, omnes reprobati rejiciuntur a gratia praedestinatorum ex libertate Dei, de suo quod vult facientis.
